scope: Entry-specific primary-text review of eight direct-looking complement records and three ambiguous antibody-sequence records. No whole-census conclusion.
evidenceBoundary: Primary prose and construct/sample/deposition information; complete frozen polymer inventories and canonical sequences. Native coordinates, structural figures, predictor results and holdout labels are excluded.

sources.title: Structure-guided discovery of a single-domain antibody agonist against human apelin receptor
sources.reviewMethod: Primary publication prose, reagent/construct methods and deposition text; no figure or coordinate file opened.

roleAndConstructEvidence.section: Generation of a potent sdAb antagonist JN241 against human APJ; APJ-JN241 complex formation and crystallization; Data and materials availability
roleAndConstructEvidence.fact: JN241 was isolated as an APJ-binding camel single-domain antibody and characterized as an antagonist. Soluble JN241 was mixed with purified engineered APJ for crystallization. The deposition is JN241, rather than the subsequently engineered agonist JN241-9.

sources.title: Smoothened stimulation by membrane sterols drives Hedgehog pathway activity.
sources.reviewMethod: Primary publication prose, reagent/construct methods and deposition text; no figure or coordinate file opened.

roleAndConstructEvidence.section: Main text, nanobody selection and crystallization preparation; Methods / Expression and purification of SMO; Data availability
roleAndConstructEvidence.fact: NbSmo8 was selected for binding active SMO. The crystallization sample combines truncated mouse SMO with SAG21k and separately expressed NbSmo8. The authors describe this receptor as lacking fusion insertions and thermostabilizing or deglycosylation mutations.

sources.title: Molecular mechanism of human α1A-adrenoceptor inhibition by Mamba snake toxin AdTx1
sources.reviewMethod: Primary publication prose, reagent/construct methods and deposition text; no figure or coordinate file opened.

roleAndConstructEvidence.section: Results / Complex formation and structure determination of the AdTx1-alpha1AAR-Nb6; Methods / alpha1AAR construct design; Data availability
roleAndConstructEvidence.fact: The alpha1AAR construct carries a KOR ICL3 segment, V256 to R270, replacing alpha1AAR positions 5.68 to 6.31 to create Nb6 recognition. AdTx1, the engineered receptor and Nb6 were prepared together. The paper explicitly deposits 8HN1, resolving the absent citation in frozen metadata.

sources.title: Structural insights into the activation and inhibition of CXC chemokine receptor 3.
sources.reviewMethod: Primary publication prose, reagent/construct methods and deposition text; no figure or coordinate file opened.

roleAndConstructEvidence.section: Results / Overall structures of CXCR3 complexes; Methods / Design and expression of constructs; Data availability
roleAndConstructEvidence.fact: CXCR3 residues 241 to 254 are replaced by KOR residues 252 to 273. Nb6 recognizes the transplanted KOR ICL3 and serves in the SCH546738 complex preparation. The receptor additionally has N-terminal BRIL. The deposition statement specifically assigns 8HNN to this construct.

sources.title: Structure basis for the modulation of CXC chemokine receptor 3 by antagonist AMG487.
sources.reviewMethod: Primary publication prose, reagent/construct methods and deposition text; no figure or coordinate file opened.

roleAndConstructEvidence.section: Main text, receptor preparation paragraph; Data availability
roleAndConstructEvidence.fact: The authors replace CXCR3 ICL3 with KOR ICL3 and couple the resulting receptor to Nb6 in AMG487. The corresponding deposition is 8K2W. This engineered-recognition strategy parallels the separately reviewed SCH546738 preparation.

sources.title: Stepwise activation of a metabotropic glutamate receptor.
sources.reviewMethod: Primary publication prose, reagent/construct methods and deposition text; no figure or coordinate file opened.

roleAndConstructEvidence.section: Introduction; Methods / Purification of Nb43; Cryo-EM sample preparation and data acquisition; Data availability
roleAndConstructEvidence.fact: Nb43 is an allosteric mGlu5 nanobody purified separately; its SUMO tag is removed before final purification. Nanodisc mGlu5 was prepared with Quis and Nb43, or Quis/CDPPB and Nb43. The deposition statement lists 8T7H, 8T8M, 8TAO and 8T6J; individual labels below use frozen entry metadata.

correctionReview.scope: The correction adds an omitted NIH acknowledgement; it does not amend the reagent or deposition statements used here.

sources.title: Bitopic Ligands Support the Presence of a Metastable Binding Site at the beta2 Adrenergic Receptor.
sources.reviewMethod: Primary citation identified; article methods and exact deposition statement were not accessible. No binder-role claim is supplied by this source.

sources.title: Cryo-EM structure of G-protein-coupled receptor GPR17 in complex with inhibitory G protein.
sources.reviewMethod: Primary methods and deposition prose; no structural images or coordinates.

facts.section: Cloning and purification of GPR17-Gi complex
facts.fact: The methods specify a full-length human GPR17 construct, dominant-negative G-alpha-i1, and G-beta1/gamma2. Purified receptor/G-protein material was incubated with antibody fragment scFv16 at a 1:1.5 molar ratio before final size-exclusion purification.
The GPR17/Gi sample is linked explicitly to PDB 7Y89 and EMDB EMD-33682.

sources.title: Molecular recognition and activation mechanism of short-chain fatty acid receptors FFAR2/3.
sources.reviewMethod: Primary correspondence preparation and exact deposition prose reviewed; supplementary construct methods remain unreviewed. No structural images or coordinates inspected.

facts.section: Main correspondence text; paragraph introducing complex preparation
facts.fact: The authors report stabilization of the FFAR2C/FFAR3C receptor-Gi complexes using NanoBiT and a single-chain antibody designated scFv16.

The paper assigns 8J24/EMD-35944 to the acetic-acid FFAR2C sample, 8J22/EMD-35942 to TUG-1375 FFAR2C, 8J21/EMD-35941 to butyric-acid FFAR3C, and 8J20/EMD-35940 to the valeric-acid/AR420626 FFAR3C sample.

limitations: Supplementary construct-design methods have not been inspected. NanoBiT use is established, but exact mapping of engineered terminal residues is not established in this review.

sources.title: Molecular recognition of niacin and lipid-lowering drugs by the human hydroxycarboxylic acid receptor 2.
sources.reviewMethod: Primary-publisher text visible in search results; incomplete primary-source review

facts.section: Publisher-indexed preparation text; exact full-text section unverified
facts.fact: A publisher-indexed excerpt names scFv16 as a single-chain antibody fragment added to stabilize nucleotide-free HCAR2-Gi samples.

facts.section: Publisher-indexed data-availability text; exact full-text section unverified
facts.fact: A publisher-indexed deposition excerpt lists PDB 8J6L, 8J6I and 8J6J and associates 8J6L with the niacin sample. Frozen metadata independently provides the same primary DOI for each.

limitations: Full text could not be retrieved: publisher web access returned 403 and direct HTTP requests timed out; Europe PMC records no PMCID/full text.
Exact receptor construct and fusion composition remains unverified.

sources.title: Development of an antibody fragment that stabilizes GPCR/G-protein complexes
sources.reviewMethod: Primary methods and deposition prose; no structural images or coordinates.

facts.section: Methods: Monoclonal antibody production and characterization
facts.fact: The authors distinguish the monoclonal-antibody heavy and light chains and describe scFv16 as a single-chain variable fragment derived from mAb16.
The mAb16-derived fragment is reported to stabilize GPCR/G-protein complexes.

limitations: This is reagent-format evidence; it does not independently establish identity or exclusion of a newly examined deposited polymer. No claim of full-length identity to the 2018 construct is made.
